definitions.explanation: A structure built into a wall where a fire can be lit for warmth. While not common in typical Japanese homes, fireplaces appear in Western-style buildings, lodges, and are familiar through foreign movies and literature.

examples.japanese: {暖炉|だんろ}に{火|ひ}をつける。
examples.english: To light a fire in the fireplace.

examples.japanese: {暖炉|だんろ}の{前|まえ}で{本|ほん}を{読|よ}む。
examples.english: To read a book in front of the fireplace.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}になると、{暖炉|だんろ}のある{山小屋|やまごや}で{過|す}ごすのが{楽|たの}しみだ。
examples.english: In winter, I look forward to spending time in a mountain lodge with a fireplace.

notes: Traditional Japanese homes use different heating methods such as {囲炉裏|いろり} (open hearth sunk into the floor) and こたつ (heated table). {暖炉|だんろ} specifically refers to the Western-style fireplace built into a wall with a chimney. Common collocations: {暖炉|だんろ}に{火|ひ}をつける (to light the fireplace), {暖炉|だんろ}の{前|まえ} (in front of the fireplace), {暖炉|だんろ}の{火|ひ} (the fire in the fireplace).
